# Principal Ride Control Software Engineer (Controls Automation) — Walt Disney Imagineering

---

**Job ID:** 10144760
**Date Posted:** Jul. 29, 2026
**Date Applied:** Jul 31, 2026
**Salary Range:** $188,400 – $252,600 / year (hiring range, Glendale, CA)

---

## Job Summary

Walt Disney Imagineering role on the Executive Ride Software Engineering team, working on large-scale, fail-safe, human-rated ride control systems. Full-time, primarily Glendale, CA, with up to ~20% travel/relocation for installation and testing at domestic and international facilities.

---

## What You'll Do

- Define, analyze, and validate deterministic solutions for large-scale, fail-safe motion control systems (system definition, performance analysis, control system architecture, detailed design specs, hazard analysis, test strategies/plans).
- Specify, design, and implement operator-intensive, safety-critical control software using real-time operating systems (theory of operation, software design docs, debug/integration test).
- Install, integrate, and test high-capacity, human-rated control systems domestically and overseas (I/O checkout, system functions testing, fault testing, tuning, acceptance testing with earned-value tracking).

### Required Qualifications
- 10+ years of experience in the software engineering field
- Software development tools experience (IDE, compilers, linkers, debuggers)
- Understanding of C++
- Understanding of or experience with Ladder Logic and Structured Text
- Expert ability to present to executive leadership; strong analytical, self-motivated, verbal, and technical-writing skills
- Willing to travel/relocate up to ~20%

Preferred: Ride Control/Theme Park experience, UML proficiency, Control Theory.

### Education
Bachelor's degree (B.S./B.A.) in Engineering, Computer Science, or Math from an accredited institution, OR a valid and current PE license.

### Benefits
Disney's standard rewards package: health and savings benefits, educational opportunities, bonus and/or long-term incentive units depending on level, plus the full range of medical/financial benefits described at jobs.disneycareers.com/benefits.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Jul 31, 2026

- **Strong overlap:** hands-on controls & automation background — Allen Bradley PLCs, automation equipment development, and hazard/risk analysis performed for ICARUS/ICARUS-Lite/ProteorPrint against EU and U.S. machinery-directive standards, which maps directly onto this role's "Hazard Analysis" and safety-critical software duties. Technical writing and documentation is an explicit skill.
- **Gap:** the listing asks for 10+ years specifically *in the software engineering field*. At this point my professional engineering experience runs from May 2020 (Engineering Technician) to present — about 5 years — and it's electromechanical/controls engineering with heavy software crossover (LabVIEW, ERP/CRM development), not a decade in a dedicated software engineering track.
- **Gap:** no direct evidence of C++ in my background; PLC work (Ladder Logic-adjacent) is the closer match to "Structured Text."
- **Gap:** no ride control or theme park industry experience (this is only a preferred qualification, not required).

### Now — Aug 22, 2026

No material change since application — `skills.json` hasn't been touched since Jul 23, 2026, so the same strengths and gaps above still hold. The years-of-experience gap narrows naturally over time regardless of site edits.

## About the Company

Walt Disney Imagineering (WDI), founded in 1952 as WED Enterprises to build Disneyland, is the creative-and-technical arm that designs and builds every Disney park, resort, attraction, and cruise ship worldwide, blending storytelling with cutting-edge engineering across 100+ disciplines. This posting sits under Walt Disney Parks and Resorts U.S., Inc., part of The Walt Disney Company's Disney Experiences segment.
